This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 16.08.2023 at about 8.45 a.m. when the petitioner was a pedestrian on the extreme left side on 1st Main Road, Near Shiva Medicals, Cholarapalya, Bengaluru (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5641/2023 City, at that time suddenly the rider of Yamaha R-15 bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right i.e. wrong side and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to such impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Sharavathi Hospitals Private Limited, RPC Layout, Vijayanagar 2nd Phase, Bangalore wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 16.8.2023 to 19.8.2023 and petitioner underwent surgery i.e. open reduction and internal fixation with locking plating under brachial block on 17.8.2023 and so far spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges, etc.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.5641/2023 healthy, doing house keeping cum coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210.
The Magadi traffic police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the rider of the said offending vehicle.

The first respondent being the R.C.Owner and the second respondent being the insurer of the Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner constrained to file a petition.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court remained absent hence, placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the objections to main petition.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable either (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5641/2023 in law or on facts.

Further respondent denies Siddamma vs Lokesh .R on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19405772/
2 all the allegations made in the petition.
Further respondent admitted the issuance of an Insurance policy in respect of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210.

Further contended that, rider of the vehicle has not valid and effective riding licence at the time of accident and the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of petition averments in toto and also denied the manner of accident.
Further contended that, accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner as she was crossing the road without having proper look out of vehicular movements.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner.
Further submits that, complaint lodged after lapse of 1 days.
Further submits that, the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.

On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner prove that she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 16.08.2023 at about 8.45 a.m, on 1st Main Road, near Shiva Medicals, Cholarapalya, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of rider of Yamaha bearing registration No.KA-02-KL-2210 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If, so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner herself examined as PW.1, One Medical Record In-charge has examined as PW.2 and Dr.Nagaraj.B.N has examined as PW.3 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 24.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led its side evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.5641/2023 the citation reported in:
- 2011-1- Supreme Court Cases 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another)
- 2023 (2) Kar.L.J.288 (Naushad Vs. M/s.IFFCO - TOKIO General Insurance Company Ltd., and another) Learned counsel for the 2nd respondent has relied upon the citation reported in:
ILR 2003 KAR 1104 (Koosappa Poojari Vs. K.Sadabba and Others).

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
-:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 16.08.2023 at about 8.45 a.m. when she was a pedestrian on the extreme left side on 1st Main Road, Near Shiva Medicals, Cholarapalya, Bengaluru City,

at that time suddenly the rider of Yamaha R-15 bearing Reg.No.KA-02- (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.5641/2023 KL-2210 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right i.e. wrong side and dashed against her.
Due to such impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner herself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief- examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

She has also got marked FIR,
complaint, police intimation, crime details, sketch, notice under Section 133 of MV Act, reply to notice, IMV report, statement, wound certificate, charge sheet, discharge summary, inpatient service receipts, prescriptions, medical bills, Aadhar and PAN cards and X-rays in all marked at Ex.P1 to P18.
10.
I have perused Ex-P1 to Ex-P8 and Ex.P.11.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 16.08.2023 at about 8.45 am., and the FIR in (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5641/2023 crime No.0109/2023 came to be registered at Magadi Road Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC, u/s.134 (a&b) of MV Act.
Further the records reveals that, petitioner herself has lodged the complaint on 17.08.2023 i.e., next day of accident marked at Ex.P.2.

Ex.P.3 is the police intimation by the Sharavathi Hospital wherein it has mentioned that, alleged history of RTA - hit by two wheeler bearing No.KA-02-KL-2210 on 16.08.2023 at 8.45 am., Ex.P.4 is the crime details form,
Ex.P.5 is the sketch which shows the spot of accident, Ex.P.6 is the notice u/s. 133 of MV Act which has given to the respondent No.1/rider of the offending motor cycle to produce vehicular documents, Ex.P.7 is the reply to notice which describe that, rider i.e., respondent No.1 was holding valid DL and vehicular particulars and policy was valid as on the date of accident, Ex.P.8 is the IMV report which discloses the right side break lever scratch noticed to the vehicle bearing No.KA-02-KL-2210 i.e., offending (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5641/2023 vehicle herein, Ex.P.9 is statement of rider of the motor cycle about the accident.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In her cross-examination she has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that, due to the negligent crossing of the road without observing vehicular movements by her, the alleged accident got occurred.

PW.1 denied the Siddamma vs Lokesh .R on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19405772/
4 same.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve her version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.11 filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence by the rider of Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA- 02-KL-2210 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: PW.1 has (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5641/2023 contended that due to the accident she sustained fracture of distal radius of ulnar styloid, right side injury symphysis pubic rami fracture, L2 compression fracture and severe injuries to legs, head and other grievous injuries to her and she underwent surgery i.e., Open reduction and internal fixation with locking plating under brachial block on 17.08.2023.

In order to prove injuries caused to her, PW.1 has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.10 which reveals that, petitioner sustained right distal radius fracture with styloid fracture, right inferior pubic rami fracture, L2 compression fracture and doctor opined that, said injury as grievous in nature and petitioner underwent surgery for right radius.

In proof of the same, petitioner examined Medical Record In-charge as PW.2 and through him got marked authorisation letter, police intimation, MLC extract and case sheet marked at Ex.P.19 to Ex.P.22.
Petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.3 and (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.5641/2023 he has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
With regard to the medical expenses, petitioner has produced 23 prescriptions marked at Ex.P.14 and 19 medical bills marked at Ex.P.15.
On perusal of Ex.P.15 - 19 medical bills it amounts to Rs.88,753/-.
Hence, in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.88,800/- (rounded off) towards Medical expenses.

Siddamma vs Lokesh .R on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19405772/
5 c)
Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
Petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.12.
On perusal of the same, she took treatment as an inpatient (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5641/2023 from 16.08.2023 to 19.08.2023 for a period of 4 days.
The petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 5 days and by including towards conveyance, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment,
conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
PW.1 has contended that she was doing house keeping work cum coolie and earning of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Petitioner has not produced any document to prove her income.
Therefore, in the absence of positive documents regarding her income, this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.,
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2023 treated as Rs.16,000/-

p.m. Considering the age, nature of injuries,
treatment given & duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation normally for at least 3 months.
Thus, by taking into account the notional income of PW.1, this Tribunal awards Rs.48,000/- (16,000/- X 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.

e) Towards Loss of Income due to Disability: PW.1 has examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N,
Orthopaedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center as PW.3 and through him got marked clinical note and one X-ray at Ex.P.23 and Ex.P.24.

PW.3 has submitted that,
a patient by name Mrs.Siddamma aged 65 years came to me on 29.07.2025 for assessment of disability with an alleged H/O RTA on 16.08.2023 and sustained right distal radius + styloid fracture, inferior pubic rami fracture, L2 compression fracture.

Further submitted that, as per the copy of the discharge summary the petitioner was treated at (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.5641/2023 Sharavathi Hospital with open reduction internal fixation with locking plating on 17.08.2025 and later discharged on 19.08.2023 with regular follow up treatment.

Further submitted that, on examination the petitioner has severe tenderness in the back, restricted spinal movements with weakness in the lower limb, restricted right wrist movements with are painful and as per recent X-ray of the right wrist shows united fracture with implant in-situ & X-ray of the DL spine shows unstable L1 compression fracture.
PW.3 further submitted that, the petitioner was examined clinically, radiologically and assessment of disability of right upper limb, ARM component and hand component.
PW.3 assessed total disability of the right arm at 35%, spinal disability at 20% and 29% whole body physical disability.
During cross examination, PW.3 deposed that, he has not given treatment to the petitioner, fracture is united with implants in situ.

By looking into the record it seems (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.5641/2023 Siddamma vs Lokesh .R on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19405772/
6 that PW.3 has assessed whole body disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 18% whole body disability which cannot be ruled out.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.16 - Aadhar card to prove her age.
As per which she was born on 10.05.1963.
Therefore, it has considered that, she was aged about 60 years as on the date of accident.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 60 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "9" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
16,000 x 12 x 9 x 18% = Rs.3,11,040/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.3,11,040/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities:
(SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.5641/2023 Petitioner contending that, due to the accident, she complains of pain in the back, unable to lift weights in the right hand and do her routine work as before.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
injuries sustained by the petitioner and by considering the age of petitioner, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) Towards future medical expenses: Petitioner has not claimed for future medical expenses.
Therefore, awarding compensation under the head future medical expenses does not arise.

12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

13. Regarding Liability: It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, petitioner was contributed to the cause of accident, as the petitioner was crossing the road unmindfully.
In addition to the same, learned counsel for the 2nd respondent relied upon the citation reported in ILR 2003 KAR 1104 (Koosappa Poojari Vs. K.Sadabba and Others).

sentences.text: But mere contention, Respondent No.2 has not taken any steps to prove the contributory negligence of petitioner.
Moreover respondent No.2 also failed to disprove the negligence of the rider of Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210.
As discussed at issue No.1 the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.5641/2023 of offending Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Yamaha R-15 bearing reg.No.KA-02-KL-2210 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation of .5,57,840/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .5,57,840/- (Rupees five lakhs fifty seven thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5641/2023 at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .5,57,840/- (Rupees five lakhs fifty seven thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5641/2023 at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
